name: כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם
summary: The king of Aram-naharaim into whose hand Yahweh sold Israel for eight years when they served the Baals and the Asherahs, until Othniel son of Kenaz, on whom the spirit of Yahweh came, judged Israel and prevailed over him. The second part of the name is the dual of רִשְׁעָה “wickedness”: “double wickedness”. Whether he bore it or the narrator named him so, the text gives it as his name both times it names him.

evidence.note: “He sold them into the hand of כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם king of Aram-naharaim, and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.”
“Yahweh gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.”
The evil Israel did: they forgot Yahweh and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
רִשְׁעָה, “wickedness, guilt”, of which רִשְׁעָתַיִם is the dual.

note: BDB key k.az.af. The first element כּוּשַׁן is left unexplained: it may be tied to כּוּשׁ or to the Cushan beside Midian in Hab 3:7 (a place, Cushan@Hab.3.7), but nothing in the text settles it. The dual reading of רִשְׁעָתַיִם is the word's own form; the name entry does not decide whether it is a by-name.
